A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods, theoretical results, simulations, and Appendices A–H. The text, equations, algorithms, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original synthetic poly-forest recovery experiments for Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric distributions, with SHD and precise recovery rate results in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: V2 retains the original simulation results in Section 6, Appendix H, and Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: PC-tree, the orientation procedure, and the distribution-specific CI tests are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the implementation procedures in Appendix H retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric poly-forest recovery tasks. No datasets, distribution families, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Both evaluate PC-tree using the same distribution-specific CI tests. Neither version introduces competing structure-learning methods into the reported experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix H retains the graph-generation procedure, sample-size sweeps, node counts, CI cutoffs, discretization, and UCI permutation settings. The replication-count correction does not introduce a different evaluation design.

E4.justification: The recovery analyses across sample sizes and graph sizes are unchanged, including the Appendix H results. No ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 6 changes the reported replication count from 20 to 50, matching Appendix H, which already states 50 in both versions. This resolves inconsistent reporting without establishing that additional runs occurred. Standard-deviation reporting in Figure 1 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 contain identical plotted results, including SHD error bars and precise recovery rate curves. The accompanying findings are retained, with no new or revised empirical result entries.

T1.justification: Definitions 3–4 clarify error control and minimum sample size, Appendix B.1 rewrites the same Bernoulli class, and Appendix C explicitly identifies existing constants as independent of sample size. These clarify existing mathematics; the assumptions, bounds, constructions, and proofs retain their substance.

C1.justification: The minimax connection between CI testing and poly-forest learning, its three distributional applications, and optimality of PC-tree remain the central claims. Adding 'minimax' in the contribution list and rephrasing the conclusion do not change their meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 adds explicit guidance on choosing dependence measures for user-defined models when suitable CI tests have provable error guarantees. This elaborates applicability of the existing framework; interpretations of the rates and the limitation to poly-forests remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H changes the experiment-code hyperlink target from OptimalPolyforests-5F64 to OptimalPolyforests-9B7D. Implementation settings and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether repository contents or accessibility changed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive novelty positioning are retained. Section 1.2 clarifies the existing comparison among undirected trees, poly-forests, and general DAGs; additional citation placements in Section 2.1 reuse already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits to the contributions, related work, definitions, and conclusion, and expands explanatory prose in Section 2.1. Section organization remains intact. It also introduces duplicated, malformed text in the Meinshausen–Bühlmann reference.

P2.justification: The Bernoulli class display in Appendix B.1 is reformatted, and altered page breaks split Definition 2 and leave the conclusion continuing onto a mostly empty page. Figures 1–2 retain identical graphics, axes, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: Correcting the replication-count inconsistency between Section 6 and Appendix H and clarifying key definitions modestly improve reporting and readability. These gains outweigh localized presentation regressions, including the malformed Meinshausen–Bühlmann reference and awkward page breaks. The scientific results and proofs remain unchanged.
